themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 24 this week, up 215% from the 7.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.46), marking a sudden acceleration of environmental violations in Tottenville/Great Kills that aligns with the community board's repeated budget requests for increased enforcement.
evidence: 24 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs 7.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (215% spike)
Z-score of 4.46 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has requested increased illegal dumping enforcement for multiple years—unresolved systemic issue
reporting_angles: Why is illegal dumping accelerating now? Interview DSNY about enforcement capacity and hotspots
Are specific neighborhoods (Tottenville vs Great Kills subsections) more affected? Map the complaints geographically

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 4 this week, a 3100% increase from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72, the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset), indicating either a sudden environmental hazard or a new pattern of properties falling into severe disrepair.
evidence: 4 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 average (3100% spike, highest z-score at 11.72)
Baseline was nearly zero—this represents a complete departure from normal patterns
Active ULURP applications (South Shore Industrial Center, 4450 Arthur Kill Road) suggest development pressure or industrial/commercial disrepair
reporting_angles: Locate the 4 affected lots—are they adjacent or scattered? Do they represent illegal dumping sites, vacant development land, or property abandonment?
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection and Department of Sanitation about which lots triggered complaints and what enforcement actions are underway

themes_detail.label: Root and Sewer Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 20 last week, a 158% increase from the 7.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.14), signaling accelerating underground infrastructure problems that align with the community board's long-standing request for sanitary sewer capital projects in underserved street segments.
evidence: 20 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs 7.8 weekly average (158% spike, z-score: 5.14)
Community board budget request [01] explicitly requests DEP capital project to develop sanitary sewers on specific street segments—unresolved for multiple years

Amboy Road Reconstruction and Richmond Valley Road Demapping recently completed (ULURP milestones), suggesting prior infrastructure work; current spike may reflect incomplete coverage or aging systems
reporting_angles: Which street segments lack sanitary sewers per the community board budget request? Are those the same neighborhoods reporting root/sewer complaints?
Interview DEP about the timeline and budget for the requested capital project—why has this been deferred year after year?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Branches
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged to 25 last week, a 388% spike from the 5.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.52), coinciding with the community board's perennial budget request for expanded forestry and street tree maintenance services.
evidence: 25 overgrown tree/branch complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.1 weekly average (388% spike, z-score: 4.52)
Community board budget request [01] requests forestry services including street tree maintenance—indicates chronic understaffing
Damaged Tree complaints also rank in top 10 (413 over 90 days), showing cumulative tree health crisis
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks about staffing levels for district 503—are crews understaffed or delayed on maintenance cycles?
Are overgrown branches creating safety hazards (sightline obstruction, pedestrian injury risk)? Document with photos from affected streets

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Going Missing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 5 this week, a 567% increase from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.39), suggesting either systematic theft, vandalism, or deferred maintenance that could impair navigation and road safety.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score: 4.39)
Baseline was nearly zero—this is a new or sudden escalation
Community board budget request [01] requests DOT street reconstruction, suggesting broader street infrastructure deficits
reporting_angles: Are the missing signs concentrated in specific neighborhoods or intersections? Interview NYPD about any reported sign theft or vandalism
Contact DOT to confirm whether this represents maintenance backlog or an uptick in theft—and what timeline exists for replacement
